fields.name: form_factor
description: Rigid board: stiff insulation sheets, typically cut to size (e.g., PIR boards, XPS boards).
Panel: prefabricated flat units, sometimes with facings or integrated layers.
Roll: flexible insulation supplied in large continuous rolls (often fiberglass or mineral wool).
Batt: semi-rigid rectangular pieces, usually sized to fit between studs or joists.
Blanket: flexible sheets, often thicker or wider than batts, used for large area coverage.
Pipe section: pre-formed cylindrical pieces designed to insulate pipes.
Loose fill: free-flowing material installed by pouring or blowing (e.g., cellulose, mineral wool granules).
Spray applied: insulation sprayed in place, expanding or curing on site (e.g., spray foam, spray-applied cellulose).
Sandwich panel: structural element with insulation core bonded between rigid facings.
Multilayer system: combination of different insulation layers or materials assembled as a unit.

fields.name: insulation_type
description: Bio-based: derived from living or once-living organisms
(e.g., cellulose, sheep's wool, cork, hemp, flax, cotton, wood fiber).
Mineral: derived from naturally occurring minerals
(e.g., fiberglass, mineral wool, perlite, vermiculite).
Synthetic: petroleum-derived insulation materials
(e.g., PUR, PIR, EPS, XPS, phenolic foam).
Composite: a mix of two or more categories
(e.g., wood fiber + PUR facing, or mineral wool with polymer binder).
Unknown: origin not specified in the EPD, and cannot be inferred.

fields.name: thermal_conductivity
description: Thermal conductivity (λ): a measure of heat flow through a material.
Lower values indicate better insulation performance.
Expressed in watts per meter-kelvin (W/mK).

fields.name: compressive_load_capacity
description: Compressive strength: ability of insulation to resist deformation under load.
Low: suitable where little or no mechanical load is applied (e.g., cavity wall fill).
Medium: adequate for moderate loads (e.g., wall panels, light roof decks).
High: supports significant loads without crushing (e.g., under screeds, flat roofs).
Need to define compresssive strength buckets for discretization

fields.name: fire_retardant
description: If the insulation explicitly uses fire retardants to improve fire performance.
usually found within bio-based and synthetic insulation types.

fields.name: sound_insulation
description: If the insulation is commonly used for sound insulation.
or if the insulation is specifically designed for acoustic performance.

fields.name: installation_method
description: Adhesive: bonding insulation to surfaces with glue or adhesive compounds.
Mechanical fixing: using screws, nails, or other fasteners to hold insulation in place.
Friction fit: insulation held in place by compression or tension between framing members (common for batts/blankets).
Gravity: relying on the weight of the insulation itself to stay in place (e.g., loose fill).
Spray applied: spraying insulation material directly onto surfaces where it adheres and expands.
Other: any other method not covered by the above categories.

fields.name: water_vapour_resistant
description: If this insulation material is renowned for its resistance to water vapour.
or if the data explicitly states that it is especially water vapour resistant.
